opts: A hypersensitivity reaction (T₄ mediated) causing reversible AKI
An ischemic injury of the proximal tubule
items.exp: AIN: hypersensitivity reaction (T₄ mediated), causing reversible AKI. (Book p799)

items.q: Fill up: AIN is a ______ reaction, T₄ mediated, causing reversible AKI.
items.exp: AIN is a hypersensitivity reaction that is T₄ mediated and produces reversible AKI. (Book p799)

items.q: Match the AIN clinical features — 1) Rash, eosinophilia  2) Renal failure  3) Edema and hypertension  4) Flank pain, haematuria, pyuria … A) Asymptomatic  B) Absent  C) Rare  D) Present with eosinophilia
items.exp: AIN clinical features: rash and eosinophilia; renal failure may be asymptomatic; no edema or HTN; flank pain, haematuria and pyuria are rare. (Book p799)

items.q: Edema and hypertension are characteristically absent in acute interstitial nephritis.
opts: True — AIN presents with neither oedema nor HTN
False — oedema is the rule in AIN
False — hypertension is the earliest sign of AIN
items.exp: AIN clinical features: no edema, no HTN (in contrast with glomerular and volume-overload AKI). (Book p799)

items.q: A patient started on an antibiotic 10 days ago now has a maculopapular rash, eosinophilia and a rising creatinine with no oedema or hypertension. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: AIN: hypersensitivity reaction with rash and eosinophilia, asymptomatic renal failure without oedema/HTN (maculopapular rash figure). (Book p799)

items.q: Match the AIN investigations — 1) RFT  2) Urinalysis  3) Renal biopsy … A) Interstitial infiltrates with a normal glomerulus  B) Impaired  C) Mild proteinuria with occasional WBC casts
items.exp: AIN investigations: impaired RFT; urinalysis — mild proteinuria with occasional WBC casts; renal biopsy — interstitial infiltrates with a normal glomerulus. (Book p799)

items.q: The renal biopsy finding in acute interstitial nephritis is:
opts: Interstitial infiltrates with a normal glomerulus
Crescentic proliferation of parietal epithelial cells
items.exp: Renal biopsy in AIN: interstitial infiltrates + normal glomerulus. (Book p799)

items.q: Fill up: The urinalysis in AIN shows mild proteinuria and occasional ______ casts.
items.exp: Urinalysis in AIN: mild proteinuria with occasional WBC casts (not RBC or muddy brown casts). (Book p799)

items.q: The treatment of acute interstitial nephritis consists of:
opts: Stop the insult, then steroids (the mainstay) after 1 week
Continue the drug with high-dose diuretics
items.exp: Treatment of AIN: stop the insult; after 1 week, steroids (mainstay). (Book p799)

items.q: In the treatment of AIN, steroids are started after:
items.exp: AIN treatment: stop the insult, and after 1 week steroids are the mainstay — the delay allows spontaneous recovery from the hypersensitivity. (Book p799)

items.q: All but one of the following are features of AIN. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Interstitial infiltrates with normal glomeruli on biopsy
items.exp: AIN is characterised by the absence of oedema and HTN; rash, eosinophilia, WBC casts and interstitial infiltrates with normal glomeruli all belong to AIN. (Book p799)
